records.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: detailed realistic 3D exploded mechanical teaching illustration near the beginning of a 2011 U.S. Toyota Camry 2.5L non-hybrid front wheel bearing DIY guide.
Input image: the supplied Toyota-style black-and-white exploded catalog diagram is a PART-INVENTORY AND COMPOSITION REFERENCE ONLY. Make new original realistic artwork; do not reproduce its numeric codes, logos or line drawing.
Primary request: ONE clean wide landscape image with ONLY the component families visible in that reference, showing how they share the hub axis and fit together. Neutral pale gray studio backdrop, realistic machined steel, cast metal, rubber boot, crisp readable external labels, generous spacing, restrained teal dotted alignment guides. An exploded conceptual assembly, not an operating tool setup.
Inventory: (1) a PARTIAL outer CV joint and splined axle stub at far left matching the cropped axle reference; do NOT add the complete half shaft. (2) exactly one thin stamped-metal inboard bearing dust deflector. (3) exactly one open internal retaining snap ring with small plier lugs. (4) exactly one double-row sealed wheel bearing, a steel annulus, clearly distinct from the hub. (5) exactly one BARE hub: a round five-hole wheel-stud flange with a leftward tubular stem and internally splined central bore. (6) exactly ONE separate representative wheel stud offset above the hub, with a short serrated press-fit base and threaded shank, its dotted insertion line points into one stud hole. Leave all five flange stud holes empty so this is a parts inventory and not a duplicate stud. (7) exactly one vented brake rotor to the right of the hub, with five wheel-stud clearance holes and a wide central hole. (8) exactly one collared twelve-point axle nut at far right along the central axle axis; clearly NOT a wheel lug nut.
Composition: INBOARD on left, OUTBOARD on right. The partial CV stub points right. Bearing and deflector, snap ring, hub neck, rotor center and axle nut share a single perspective-correct common axis. The snap ring belongs to a knuckle groove that is NOT included in this limited picture; the small deflector is NOT the broad brake shield. Stagger exploded items enough to read them, preserve physically sensible relative sizes. Hub stem fits through bearing inner rings; rotor fits over the hub flange and its five-stud pattern. Do not imply rotor contacts bearing or snap ring fits a shaft groove.
Exact text, short separate leader labels only: "INBOARD", "OUTBOARD", "Outer CV joint / axle stub", "Bearing dust deflector", "Bearing snap ring", "Wheel bearing", "Hub", "Wheel stud: one shown", "Brake rotor", "Axle nut". Bottom caption: "Exploded parts map: knuckle housing omitted".
Constraints: no knuckle, no strut, no control arm, no tie rod, no brake caliper, no broad brake shield, no wheel, no lug nuts, no extra bearings or rings, no hands, no tools, no dimensions, no torque values, no part numbers, no step numbers, no force arrows. Photorealistic educational rendering, not a real repair photograph or verified CAD. Sharp, readable, high detail and high resolution, landscape.
corrections: Use case: precise-object-edit. Correct ONLY the counted hole patterns and snap ring in this existing exploded parts image. Keep composition, camera, materials, labels, other parts, axles, hub/rotor locations and bottom caption unchanged. The Camry hub flange must have EXACTLY FIVE wheel-stud holes on its bolt circle, spaced 72 degrees apart. The rotor hat must also have EXACTLY FIVE stud clearance holes on the corresponding five-hole bolt circle, plus its separate large center hole. The current image appears to have six: remove the sixth and redistribute the FIVE holes evenly. Keep the single detached representative wheel stud and its line pointing to one of the five hub holes. It is a FIVE-LUG passenger car, not a six-lug truck. Correct the snap ring to ONE unbroken C-shaped spring-steel internal snap ring with ONE opening and exactly TWO plier-hole eyelets, one at each tip. No third tip, no second break, no extra fragment. Keep its size, placement and existing leader label. Make no other change and add no parts or labels.

records.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: original detailed realistic 3D exploded front-corner assembly teaching illustration for an at-home U.S. 2011 Camry 2.5L non-hybrid wheel-bearing guide.
Input reference image: supplied black-and-white catalog diagram supplies the CORE PART INVENTORY and relative axle-axis relationships only. Extend it into a wider teaching view. Do not copy Toyota numeric callouts or present measured CAD.
Primary request: one landscape realistic exploded and connection-map illustration that makes it intuitive how the bearing/hub/rotor assembly meets the steering knuckle, front suspension and brake. Neutral light gray studio backdrop, clean realistic steel and casting textures, no car body or wheel, perspective about 25 degrees from outboard so hub faces remain readable, fine teal dotted assembly axes, labels around the outside. Precise parts separation and roomy composition are more important than drama.
Core axle-axis layout: left marked INBOARD, right OUTBOARD. A partial CV outer joint with boot and splined stub enters from left. On this same central axis show the small inboard bearing dust deflector, one C-shaped bearing snap ring, a sealed double-row wheel bearing, then the central STEERING KNUCKLE with an empty round bearing bore and an illustrative cutaway of its fixed shoulder/groove. The bearing is exploded just inboard of its knuckle bore, with a dotted line showing it belongs INSIDE the bore, never bolted to the outside. On the outboard face show the broad thin BRAKE DUST SHIELD behind the HUB flange, then the separate hub, separate vented BRAKE ROTOR and collared 12-point AXLE NUT at far right on the same axle centerline. Hub stem points inboard through the shield center and into the bearing inner rings. Show a FIVE-STUD passenger-car hub: EXACTLY FIVE installed wheel studs on a 72-degree circle, all five distinguishable. Rotor has EXACTLY FIVE corresponding stud holes, plus large center hole. No sixth stud or hole. The axle nut threads on the CV axle, not on the hub. Do not draw force arrows or instructional step numbers.
Surrounding connections: short lower STRUT CLEVIS above the knuckle with its two through-bolt connections indicated by dotted alignment; OUTER TIE-ROD END extending from inboard rear/left toward a separate knuckle steering arm, tapered stud and castle nut visible as one group; LOWER BALL JOINT below the knuckle, tapered stud points into lower knuckle socket, its separate flange meets a partial LOWER CONTROL ARM end using the Camry-style one-bolt/two-nut flange connection. An ABS SENSOR with short lead aligns to a small inboard knuckle sensor boss near the CV joint; do NOT show a magnetic encoder on the bearing. On the side of the rotor show a separated FRONT BRAKE CALIPER/CARRIER/PADS group, with carrier ears aligning back to knuckle mounting ears. A short flexible brake hose belongs to caliper and a small hose/wire bracket belongs to strut; do not route a hose through the bearing. Put caliper offset toward upper-right so no part obscures bearing/hub alignment.
Use concise accurate labels for these component groups: "Strut clevis", "Steering knuckle", "Outer tie rod", "Lower ball joint", "Lower control arm", "CV outer joint / axle", "ABS sensor", "Bearing dust deflector", "Bearing snap ring", "Wheel bearing", "Brake dust shield", "Hub + five wheel studs", "Brake rotor", "Caliper + carrier + pads", "Axle nut". Bottom caption: "Expanded connection map: exploded positions are illustrative".
Constraints: ONE knuckle, ONE bearing, ONE hub, ONE rotor, ONE caliper group, ONE tie rod, ONE lower ball joint, ONE control arm end, exactly FIVE hub wheel studs, no wheel/tire, no sway bar parts, no tools or people, no extra rings, no lug nuts, no numerical Toyota part codes, no torque or dimensions. A physically plausible simplified educational rendering, not an actual repair photo or vehicle-specific verified CAD. Dotted lines show mating relationships, not removal or installation order. High resolution and sharp readable labels.
corrections:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Correct mechanical mistakes in this existing expanded front-corner illustration while preserving the overall layout, material realism, colors, existing labels, all core components, and axle-axis dotted line.
1. ROTOR: its hat must contain EXACTLY FIVE equally spaced wheel-stud holes on a 72-degree bolt circle, plus its single large center opening. The current six-hole pattern is wrong. The hub must keep EXACTLY FIVE wheel studs. Do not add other holes.
2. SNAP RING: replace the fragmented-looking ring with ONE continuous C-shaped internal retaining ring, ONE opening, exactly TWO plier-hole eyelets, one at each tip. No third tip, second break or loose segment.
3. REMOVE BOTH teal dotted lines running from the two STRUT through-bolts to the BRAKE CALIPER. The strut is already correctly held to the upper knuckle with its two bolts; the caliper does NOT attach to the strut. Keep this two-bolt strut-to-knuckle assembly intact. Place the caliper/ carrier group slightly down and right, beside the rotor's outer braking ring. Show two small carrier mounting ears with a subtle bracket-style text note "Carrier mounts to knuckle" and a single fine GRAY connection leader back to the knuckle's caliper mounting ears near the outer side of the bearing housing. Do NOT draw a caliper connection to the strut, ABS sensor or rotor center. Use the gray line as a connection locator, not a physical bolt-axis drawing.
4. CORRECT LOWER BALL JOINT / ARM FLANGE: remove the invented two horizontal clevis bolts. This Camry-type lower arm connection is a FLAT HORIZONTAL flange: the ball-joint base has TWO downward vertical fixed studs passing through the overlapping stamped control-arm end, each with a nut BELOW; beside them is ONE vertical bolt through the third flange/arm hole. Render exactly those three flange fastener positions, all vertical, not an upright two-bolt clevis. Keep the lower ball-joint tapered stud pointing upward toward the knuckle. Remove the invented large threaded cap/bolt protruding directly beneath the ball joint body. Keep the labels "Lower ball joint" and "Lower control arm".
5. Give the floating outer tie rod a thin gray locator leader to its distinct knuckle steering arm/boss, separate from the ABS sensor boss. This is a relation locator only, not a force arrow. Retain generic current perspective and add no claim of exact handedness or measured coordinates.
Add no torque values, dimensions or part numbers, no wheel or tools. Keep bottom caption that the exploded positions are illustrative. Preserve readable labels.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Make only the following focused cleanup in this existing educational expanded parts map; preserve the composition, labels, five-stud hub, five-hole rotor, single C snap ring, axial exploded stack, textures and every component.
REMOVE the gray arrow/connection line that currently runs from the outer tie rod toward the ABS sensor. The tie rod does not connect to the sensor. Keep the ordinary black label leader "Outer tie rod" pointing to the rod.
REMOVE ALL gray arrows or connecting leaders attached to the note "Carrier mounts to knuckle", particularly the false line ending at the lower strut bolt. Keep the note as plain standalone text beside the caliper group with NO arrows. Keep normal black part-identification labels. Do not invent a replacement connection leader.
On the LOWER BALL JOINT / LOWER CONTROL ARM flange, REMOVE the visible large bolt heads, threaded studs and nuts used for the arm attachment. Keep the ball-joint body and upward tapered stud, and keep its flat horizontal flange mating with the stamped arm end, but deliberately omit its attachment hardware entirely. Do not add any replacement studs, nuts, clevis or bolt. The written guide separately specifies its one bolt and two nuts; this broad parts image should not portray misleading overlapping hardware. Leave clean flat mating metal with attachment holes understated or occluded by the flange overlap.
Do not modify the two strut-to-knuckle through-bolts. Do not change the caliper or its hose. No new objects, no changed labels, no force arrows or dimensions. The image remains a recognition map with simplified attachment details.
